failures.criterion: Review finding 4 as the architect set it: each refusal says what is true in the case it is reached in. A sentence that tells the reader their words are no longer where they selected them, while those words are exactly where they selected them, is the defect that finding named - now reachable through this round's own cross-block path
failures.evidence: Red test: packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts, 'a cross-block refusal does not claim the words moved while they are where they were' (commit c12eb998f5cb). Four paragraphs: 'The fox jumps.' / 'Over the lazy dog it goes.' / 'A hound also jumps.' / 'Over the lazy dog it trots.'. The reader selects across the first break ('jumps.' to 'Over the lazy dog'), so the composer keeps no block and no surroundings. Another writer rewrites the first two paragraphs around the selection ('The swift fox jumps.', 'Over the lazy dog it bounds.'), which takes the mark and leaves the reader's own words where they were; the same words read across the second pair too. Refusing is right - nothing says which pair is theirs - but the sentence shown is 'The text you selected is still in the document, but no longer where you selected it, so this comment cannot be attached on its own', and the second clause is false: their words never moved. Run `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait`: the row fails on that sentence (`expect(received).not.toContain('no longer where you selected it')`), and asserts only what must not be said, never the wording to use. In remarkRange the document-wide step answers `readings.count > 0 ? 'unplaceable' : 'gone'` whenever more than one reading is surrounded alike; with no placement every reading is 'surrounded', so two readings land on the 'elsewhere' sentence where the 'read in more than one place with the same text around them' sentence is the true one - that sentence already exists and is already correct in the block case (measured below). The architect may judge this not worth a round at the cap; it is recorded as a failure because it is the same class the review already failed once, and the fix is a routing change of one branch, not new behaviour.

environment: The pod harness is unchanged: /legion/scratch/harness/setup.sh with env.sh beside it (rootless PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector, Playwright Chromium), idempotent. One thing to know for a throwaway probe spec: Playwright runs the rows of one file in parallel workers here, and every row's `resetDatabase` truncates the database under the others, so a probe file must be run one row at a time with `-g` or its rows will wreck each other's documents - two of mine did before I noticed.
